title: add benchmark-lab memory profiling baselines and reporting pipeline
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Add memory-profiling baselines and a reporting pipeline for benchmark-lab. Motivation: teams running large-sequence workloads have reported unexplained OOM events on long-context traces and inconsistent memory scaling across model variants. This PR adds representative memory profiling workloads, a standardized baseline runner that collects per-layer peak RSS and GPU allocation traces, and a reporting pipeline that ingests profiling artifacts, aggregates metrics, and publishes a daily baseline report to the benchmarking dashboard. The change set includes: 1) workload runners (cpu/gpu) that run end-to-end traces with deterministic seeds and collect cgroups and nvprof/NVIDIA DCGM traces where available; 2) a new profiling-baselines pipeline (Airflow + lightweight lambda processor) that normalizes artifacts and stores derived metrics into the benchmark metrics bucket; 3) metrics exporter and Grafana dashboard panels for memory heatmaps and per-commit regressions; 4) docs and runbooks describing how to add new model variants to the baseline set. Testing: unit tests for artifact normalization, integration tests that run a short profile on CI (uses a small toy model) and end-to-end smoke runs on the perf-canary infra. Backwards compatibility: the pipeline is additive and uses a new S3 prefix; existing reporting and dashboards are unchanged. Rollout: default enabled for benchmark-lab, opt-out via pipeline config if teams want to avoid additional artifacts. See release_notes for UX and migration notes.

release_notes: Added memory profiling baselines and reporting pipeline for benchmark-lab. New baseline runners collect per-layer and per-device peak memory metrics; daily baseline reports available on the benchmarking dashboard. Raw traces retained 30d and compressed derived metrics retained per retention policy. To onboard a model variant: add an entry to benchmark-lab/config/representative_variants.yaml and trigger the baseline DAG.
